items.title: Why every big bank slowed down when Chase broke
items.summary: One software bug at Chase slowed payments at America's biggest banks on Monday. By about 1 p.m., more than 4,700 Chase customers had reported problems on Downdetector. Bank of America hit roughly 2,000 and Wells Fargo spiked too (Click2Houston). A payment between two banks needs both to answer, so every payment touching Chase waited in line. It was the fourth big outage in five days. Idea: TEK1o1. items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Released
items.summary: PostgreSQL 19 Released Most years PostgreSQL ships a new release in September, but this year's release came two months later thanks mainly to the flurry of issues that the PostgreSQL team needed to address as part of the ongoing AI-reported vulnerability apocalypse. This release was definitely worth the wait. My favorite new feature is this one: For applications that send reads to standbys, PostgreSQL 19 adds "read-your-writes" consistency with the new WAIT FOR LSN command. items.title: When will the Sun die?
items.summary: Our Sun is about halfway through its life. The Sun formed about 4.6 billion years ago and is a little less than halfway through its life. In about 5 billion years it becomes a red giant that swallows Mercury and Venus, with Earth the open question. Then it sheds its outer layers and leaves a white dwarf that cools for billions of years. Idea: Cleo Abram. Source: NASA Science (Sun facts, Stars). Footage: Storyblocks, NASA, and a Hubble image of the Ring Nebula (NASA, ESA, C. Robert O'Dell). The star chart is a schematic. If Earth gets swallowed, where do you go?
